description:
FILED s532d (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08), found by #3830's probes.  PRE-EXISTING (base 06a4b8ba the same).

perl's scalar() only imposes scalar context: it returns the SV, so an aliasing consumer (a sub's @_, foreach) sees the variable itself.  PCL's p-scalar returns the VALUE (`(stringp v) v`), so the alias is lost:
    sub app { $_[0] .= "Z" } my $x = "a"; app(scalar($x)); print "$x\n";            # perl aZ, PCL a
    my %h = (k => "b"); app(scalar($h{k})); print "$h{k}\n";                          # perl bZ, PCL b
(probe scratch/s532d/pr/sc.pl in the s532d worktree).  s532d made p-scalar answer a PRIVATE-BUFFER box (:strbuf / :memfh) as itself, so that one shape aliases like perl now (ir-spec "in-place .=", #3830); a dualvar box already did.  Every `($)` prototype slot is a p-scalar, so a user sub with a `$` prototype that writes $_[0] is the shape that matters.  FIX SHAPE (not designed): return the box for any scalar BOX that is not a reference wrapper when the consumer aliases; the copy for a value consumer is what box-set already does.  Measure the `($)`-slot rows (Pl/t grep `proto`) first: returning the box changes what a `($)` callee's @_ holds.


=== DONE (s536f) ===
Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08.  FIXED at the EMISSION site (p-scalar itself unchanged, as the brief asked).  `Pl::ExprToCL::_scalar_noop_operand` answers the operand of `scalar(E)` when E is a scalar lvalue (`_scalar_lvalue_node_p`: a `$` variable, an element named or through a reference, a scalar deref `$$r` / `${$r}`; nested `scalar(scalar(...))` and a paren layer seen through), and the three user-call argument sites (gen_funcall_form's argument loop, the method call, the coderef call) lower that operand exactly as the bare argument -- an element's lazy argbox (a written missing key is created, a read one is not, as perl), a raw-slot variable's copy-back (`_copy_back_args` sees through too).  A `$`-prototype slot also passes a scalar deref `$$r` as itself now (it was wrapped in p-scalar = a copy; the #2860 rule's missing shape).  Probes scratch/s536f/p/m4.pl m4b.pl m4c.pl m4d.pl.  Guard Pl/t/proto-alias-01.t row 11 (FAILS on c8886b61).  Residue filed #4685 (foreach / map / `\scalar($x)`); `f(scalar($r->{k}))` copies exactly as `f($r->{k})` does (not-supported "deref elements").

Review probes perl -> main ce06e1f6 -> tree (scratchpad p536f/a.pl b.pl c.pl, 35 lines): tree = perl on every line; main wrong on 11 and died twice (the read-only s/// on a tied element assignment, an unbound glob after (*g, *h) = LIST). No baseline row is keyed on this task.
subject: scalar(EXPR) copies a plain scalar where perl passes the SV itself: `sub f { $_[0] .= "Z" } my $x = "a"; f(scalar($x)); print $x` is aZ in perl, a in PCL (also a hash element) -- silent wrong, rare
